about: Wisconsin DPI license areas for cross-referencing postings: official titles, ELO subject codes, current (2018 PI 34) and legacy grade levels, minimum degree, tests, regex aliases for posting text, and the WECAN license names that map to each. 'infer' rules (first match wins) name the usual licenses when a posting lists none; 'routes' and 'rules' hold the plain-language alternatives and degree rules. Built 2026-10-21 from PI 34 (via Cornell LII, amended through CR 24-077), DPI testing and add-on guidance, the 2026-27 WISEstaff assignment list and DPI Choice Bulletin 05-01. Entries marked verified:false rest on secondary sources.

ec_regular.title: Early Childhood - Regular Education
tests: Foundations of Reading Test for WI (NES 190/890, pass 233) for first Tier II
ec_regular.notes: 1777 is reused: legacy MC-EA/EC-MC 'Regular Education' also = 1777; check grade range. 4K may also be taught on a K-9 license that includes PK/K.
wecan: Early Childhood – Middle Childhood Regular Education

elem_middle.title: Elementary and Middle School (regular education)
elem_middle.legacy: 1088 Elementary Ed 1-8 or 1-6; 1777 Regular Ed MC-EA (1-8) or EC-MC (birth-6)
tests: Praxis 5001 subtests RLA157/M157/SS155/S159 (OOS) or EPP GPA/portfolio
Foundations of Reading Test for WI (NES 190/890, pass 233) for first Tier II
elem_middle.notes: Self-contained any subject except world language; departmentalized ELA/math/sci/SS only (PI 34.045). Grades 7-8 graduation-credit/HS courses need content license.
wecan: Middle Childhood – Early Adolescence Regular Education

ela.title: English and Language Arts
ela.legacy: 1300 English EA-A; 1301 Broadfield Language Arts EA-A (thru gr10 + basic 11-12); 1310 Journalism; 1320 Speech Communication
ela.notes: 2300 covers English, journalism, speech; NOT a reading teacher assignment.

computer_science.title: Computer Science
computer_science.notes: Required when CS course earns math credit; other tech courses may be business (1250) / tech ed (1220) / art (1550).

science.title: Science (broad)
science.legacy: 1601 Broadfield Science EA-A (thru gr10 + basic 11-12); 1620 General Science; 1621 Science (1-9/6-9); 1600 Science(all) pre-1980
science.notes: 2600 = any science grades 4-12. 1600/1620/1627/1630/1637-type legacy codes partly obsolete (PI 34.111).

social_studies.title: Social Studies (broad)
social_studies.legacy: 1701 Broadfield Social Studies EA-A (thru gr10 + fusion 11-12); 1700 SS(all) pre-1972
social_studies.notes: 2700 = any social studies 4-12 incl. AP Gov/history; also personal financial literacy.

psychology.title: Psychology
psychology.notes: Broadfield SS (1701) and pre-1972 1700 do not cover discrete psychology courses.

world_languages.title: World Languages
tests: ACTFL OPI + WPT Intermediate High (LTI); Hmong: STAMP WS 6
world_languages.notes: ASL (assignment area 0348) code not found; 'Other World Languages' license exists. Unverified for ASL.

esl.title: English as a Second Language
esl.notes: Can be added to 2088/2801 by content test.

bilingual.title: Bilingual-Bicultural Education (supplementary)
bilingual.levels: Grade levels of the base teaching license
bilingual.notes: Supplemental: must also hold a teaching license (PI 34.078); 'Bilingual Spanish elementary' = 2088 (or 1777) + 1023 (+ Spanish proficiency).

reading_teacher.title: Reading Teacher (supplementary)
reading_teacher.degree: bachelor + base teaching license + 2 yrs classroom experience
reading_teacher.notes: Required for teaching reading >1 class/day, Title I reading, Reading Recovery outside self-contained class.

reading_specialist.title: Reading Specialist (administrator category)
reading_specialist.degree: master's (admin-category license; see PI 34.070, not downloaded) - unverified

music.title: Music
music.legacy: 1506 Instrumental EC-A; 1511 Choral EC-A; 1515 General EC-A; 1505/1510 legacy instrumental/vocal; 1500 Music(all) obsolete

dance.title: Dance
dance.notes: CR 24-008 proposed making dance obsolete (dance under PE); status unclear (scope withdrawn 2025-02-07?) - DPI site still lists Dance K-12.

tech_ed.title: Technology Education
tech_ed.notes: Experience-based Tier I tech/vocational license (PI 34.037) and trade specialist permit (PI 34.0374) are district-specific alternatives.

business_ed.title: Business Education (Business & Information Technology)
business_ed.notes: 1251 appears in DPI's What Can I Teach page (business ed variant) - meaning unverified.

library_media.title: Instructional Library Media Specialist
tests: none listed in OOS guidance - unverified

gifted.title: Gifted and Talented (teacher, supplementary)
gifted.notes: PI 34.081: license is NOT required to teach in a G&T program. Codes from UW-Whitewater, not DPI.

alternative_ed.title: Alternative Education Program (supplementary)
alternative_ed.notes: Code from CUW program page, not DPI.

montessori.title: Montessori Teacher
tests: Praxis 5018 (EC, Elem I) or 5001 (Elem II, secondary)
montessori.notes: Tier II under PI 34.040(2)(e)/s.118.194; exempt from Act 20 reading/LA requirement.

cross_cat.title: Cross-Categorical Special Education
cross_cat.legacy: 1801 at MC-EA (K-8 for SPED) or EA-A (5-12)
tests: Foundations of Reading Test or SPED FORT-alternative course (s.118.19(14)(b))
cross_cat.notes: 2801 serves ID, EBD, SLD, autism, OHI etc. (not DHH/VI/SLP services). Tier I SPED max 3 years (IDEA).

ld.title: Learning Disabilities / Specific Learning Disabilities
ld.legacy: legacy only (no new issuance under 2018 rule; new = 2801)

id_cd.title: Cognitive Disabilities / Intellectual Disabilities
id_cd.legacy: legacy only; 1806 Mild/Moderate ID, 1807 Severely Handicapped (rare)

autism.title: Autism (no separate license)
autism.legacy: WISEstaff area 0818 Autism accepts these codes
autism.notes: Wisconsin has no autism-specific teaching license.

dhh.title: Deaf or Hard of Hearing
dhh.notes: No LWS3 allowed; Tier I not allowed.

ecse.title: Early Childhood Special Education
tests: Foundations of Reading Test for WI (NES 190/890, pass 233) for first Tier II

slp.title: Speech and Language Pathology
slp.notes: Tier I path: master's + DSPS SLP license (PI 34.028(2)(d)). Licensed as a teaching license under PI 34.0475.

short_term_sub_permit.title: Three-Year Short-Term Substitute Teacher Permit (Tier I)
short_term_sub_permit.levels: Any subject/grade, <=45 consecutive days per assignment
short_term_sub_permit.degree: associate degree + approved sub training, OR age 20+ & EPP junior status + 15 hrs observation
short_term_sub_permit.notes: ELO license-type code not found (unverified). Does not satisfy Choice teacher credential.

five_year_sub.title: Five-Year (Long-Term) Substitute License (Tier I)
five_year_sub.levels: Grades/subjects of a license held or eligible; short-term anywhere
five_year_sub.degree: completed an approved EPP (or equivalent OOS license)
five_year_sub.notes: Long-term (>45 days) assignment requires license in the grade/subject, or a district-requested LWS1.

charter_school_license.title: Charter School License (teacher) - Tier I, 5-yr renewable
charter_school_license.levels: Subject/grade of license; non-virtual charter schools only
charter_school_license.legacy: replaces obsolete 'Charter School Instructional Staff' permit
charter_school_license.degree: bachelor (accredited) + major/minor or passing content test in subject
tests: Praxis content test if no major/minor
charter_school_license.notes: Exempt from Act 20 reading/LA (Tier I). Not valid in virtual charters.

wl_spanish.title: World Language – Spanish
tests: ACTFL OPI + WPT Intermediate High (LTI); Hmong: STAMP WS 6

wl_chinese.title: World Language – Chinese (Mandarin)
tests: ACTFL OPI + WPT Intermediate High (LTI); Hmong: STAMP WS 6

wl_french.title: World Language – French
tests: ACTFL OPI + WPT Intermediate High (LTI); Hmong: STAMP WS 6

wl_german.title: World Language – German
tests: ACTFL OPI + WPT Intermediate High (LTI); Hmong: STAMP WS 6

wl_hmong.title: World Language – Hmong
tests: ACTFL OPI + WPT Intermediate High (LTI); Hmong: STAMP WS 6

wl_latin.title: World Language – Latin
tests: ACTFL OPI + WPT Intermediate High (LTI); Hmong: STAMP WS 6

any_license.title: Any Wisconsin teaching license
any_license.notes: Short-term subs may hold any Wisconsin license or the substitute permit (PI 34.109).

adaptive_ed.title: Adaptive Education (special education)
adaptive_ed.notes: Code from DPI special-education aid table.

interpreter_sub.title: Educational Interpreter Substitute License
interpreter_sub.notes: Educational interpreter substitute license (45 days or less).

assignment.title: Teaching license for the assignment
assignment.notes: WECAN lists an assignment rather than a license area (e.g. Title I, academic support, teacher in charge, religious studies); a teaching license appropriate to the assignment is expected.

head_start.title: Head Start teacher credential (federal Head Start standards)
head_start.notes: Head Start and Early Head Start teachers are covered by federal staff-qualification rules (an associate or bachelor’s degree in early childhood education, or a CDA credential for infant/toddler teachers), not a DPI license.

rules.substitute: DPI’s short-term substitute permit needs at least an associate degree plus approved training, or enrollment in an educator-preparation program at junior standing.
rules.long_term: Assignments over 45 consecutive days need a license for the assignment (or a Five-Year Long-Term Substitute License), and every Wisconsin teaching license requires a bachelor’s degree.
rules.teacher: Every Wisconsin teaching license requires a bachelor’s degree.
rules.pupil_services: School counselor, speech-language pathologist and social worker licenses require a master’s degree; school psychologists need an Ed.S. or doctorate.

substitute: No license yet? The DPI short-term substitute permit needs an associate degree plus approved training; see Become a substitute.
long_term: Permit holders can cover up to 45 consecutive days. Beyond that, a district can request a One-Year License with Stipulations if you hold a bachelor’s degree and enroll in an educator-preparation program.
teacher: Bachelor’s degree but no license? Public districts, charters and private schools can request a One-Year License with Stipulations (Tier I) while you complete an educator-preparation program.
License Based on Equivalency, the ABCTE online route, and out-of-state reciprocity also lead to a Tier II license.

private: Private schools in the Parental Choice Program accept any DPI teaching license or a bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution; the short-term substitute permit doesn’t qualify.
other: Charter schools can use the Tier I Charter School License: a bachelor’s degree plus a major or minor in the subject, or a passing content test.
